# Ramen

> Multizone, highly available, enterprise-grade MCP (Model Context Protocol) server for GCP and AWS Kubernetes. A git repo of Python tools, resources and prompts becomes a fleet of MCP workers behind a cloud load balancer. A Rust node speaks Streamable HTTP (`POST /mcp`) and JSON-RPC 2.0 over gRPC on one port; a Python 3.14 runtime runs the code; a FastAPI console manages groups, environments, zones, secrets, canary deploys, roles per group, OAuth, IP rules, throttling and audit. BSD-3-Clause. Version 0.6.0.

Clients send `Authorization: Bearer rmk_<group key>` or a console-issued OAuth token, plus `ramen-group` and `ramen-zone` headers the load balancer routes on. Standard MCP clients (Claude Code, Claude Desktop, Cursor, the mcp SDK) connect directly over HTTP; stdio-only clients use `ramen-mcp-bridge` (PyPI), which carries a key or signs the person in with `--oauth`. Tools live in a git repo under `mcp/tools/<name>/<name>.py` + `<name>.json`; deploys sync the repo to a bucket, roll a canary worker, smoke-test, then roll stable.

## Docs

- [Home](https://bkraad47.github.io/ramen/): what Ramen is, the three repos, why
- [Get started](https://bkraad47.github.io/ramen/get-started/): run locally, connect an MCP repo, connect Claude with a key or OAuth, the bridge
- [How it works](https://bkraad47.github.io/ramen/how-it-works/): the architecture and every feature with where it is managed
- [Deploy on GCP](https://bkraad47.github.io/ramen/wiki/deploy-gcp/): Terraform, images, Helm, first zone and group, the console's service account and access controls, teardown
- [Deploy on AWS](https://bkraad47.github.io/ramen/wiki/deploy-aws/): the same on EKS with DynamoDB, S3, Secrets Manager and an ALB
- [Groups, zones and regions](https://bkraad47.github.io/ramen/wiki/groups-zones/): the model, deploying, scaling, rebalance, blocked packages, IP rules
- [The MCP repo](https://bkraad47.github.io/ramen/wiki/mcp-repo/): layout, the JSON contract, resources and prompts, secrets in code, local testing, worker images
- [Secrets](https://bkraad47.github.io/ramen/wiki/secrets/): scopes, `{{$group.NAME}}`, `mcp/env.yaml`, backends
- [Users and access](https://bkraad47.github.io/ramen/wiki/users-access/): roles per group, the Users page, service-account permissions, audit and logs
- [Connect with OAuth](https://bkraad47.github.io/ramen/wiki/connect-oauth/): registering a client, Claude Code, Claude Desktop, Cursor, the bridge
- [Connect with a password](https://bkraad47.github.io/ramen/wiki/connect-password/): a password account through the same flow
- [API keys and the API](https://bkraad47.github.io/ramen/wiki/api-keys/): `rmk_` versus `rmn_`, the OpenAPI page at `/api/docs`, a cheat sheet
- [Throttling with Redis](https://bkraad47.github.io/ramen/wiki/throttling/): per-IP and per-token limits shared across zones
- [Entra ID and Google Workspace](https://bkraad47.github.io/ramen/wiki/sso/): OIDC sign-in and claim-to-role rules (untested against a real tenant)
- [Backups](https://bkraad47.github.io/ramen/wiki/backups/): create, preview, restore, prune, reconcile
- [Configuration](https://bkraad47.github.io/ramen/wiki/configuration/): the config file, the state store, every variable that matters, restricting actions
- [Changelog](https://bkraad47.github.io/ramen/changelog/), [Releases](https://bkraad47.github.io/ramen/release/), [Version tracker](https://bkraad47.github.io/ramen/versions/)
- [Transport, hop by hop](https://bkraad47.github.io/ramen/wiki/transport/): what protects each hop, what is verified and what is not
- [Threat model](https://bkraad47.github.io/ramen/threat-model/)
- [Interface contracts](https://bkraad47.github.io/ramen/CONTRACTS/)
- [Architecture](https://bkraad47.github.io/ramen/architecture/): components, data model, decisions

## Code

- [ramen](https://github.com/bkraad47/ramen): console/ (FastAPI), node-rs/ (Rust, tonic), runtime-py/ (Python), proto/, deploy/ (compose, Helm, Terraform, CloudFormation), skills/, tests/
- [ramen-mcp-bridge](https://github.com/bkraad47/ramen-mcp-bridge): the stdio bridge, `pip install ramen-mcp-bridge`
- [ramen-demo-mcp-group](https://github.com/bkraad47/ramen-demo-mcp-group): the demo group repo, one tool, one resource, one prompt, an `env.yaml`
- [Releases](https://github.com/bkraad47/ramen/releases)
